Legacy contracts
Some legacy LIBOR contracts lack adequate fallback language and extend past June/uni00A02023, when the 
main tenors of USD LIBOR will cease to be published on a representative basis. In March/uni00A02021, the 
ARRC estimated outstanding legacy USD LIBOR exposures at roughly $223/uni00A0trillion. Approximately 
$74/uni00A0trillion of these legacy contracts are set to mature beyond the critical date of June/uni00A02023, and some 
of those contracts will lack adequate fallback language. Federal legislation that would address these 
contracts has been introduced in the Congress. Earlier in the year, the states of New York and Alabama 
enacted legislation that will allow legacy contracts governed by each state’s law to transition to SOFR-
based rates, but federal legislation would establish a clear and uniform solution on a nationwide basis.
